pulls.title: Clarify acceptance, failure, and withdrawal semantics
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Addresses the lifecycle and failure-semantics review of the editor's copy. One commit per finding, so any one can be dropped.

## Changes

| Commit | Finding | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Define one acceptance rule for both representations | Accepted vs. retrieved lifecycle (High) | §4.3 is now **Acceptance**: an IP range set, by value or by reference, is validated completely, accepted per local policy, and replaces the previous set in full; the accepted set stays in effect while a validated set awaits approval. §4 renamed **Retrieval and Acceptance**. |
| Revalidate with the latest response's entity tag | HTTP caching coupled to acceptance (Medium) | Conditional requests use the entity tag of the most recent complete response the consumer has retained from that URI, not the document behind the accepted set (which re-downloaded on every check while a set awaited approval); with none retained, the request is unconditional. Fresh response ≠ accepted; expiry ≠ withdrawal. |
| Keep required enforcement in effect when no set is accepted | Enforcement ambiguity (High) | A consumer that requires an accepted set for a client, and has none (no declaration, invalid or unretrievable declaration, or set awaiting approval), MUST reject requests from that client. Withdrawal rule moved next to the failure rule in §4.5. |
| Bound use of an accepted set that cannot be refreshed | Stale ranges (Medium) | Consumers SHOULD limit how long they use an accepted set while refreshes fail; stopping can narrow but not widen admission. No interval mandated. |
| Correct withdrawal through RFC 7592 client update | RFC 7592 deletion not guaranteed (Medium) | Omitting both parameters *requests* removal, which RFC 7592 §2.2 lets the authorization server ignore; the client information response shows the result. |
| Leave resource server enforcement out of scope | RS identity ambiguity (Medium) | The RS bullet no longer implies the token's client is the sender; RS enforcement, client determination, and metadata distribution are out of scope (companion specification). |
| Relate the document format to JAFAR | Related publication formats (Low) | One sentence in the Introduction and an informative reference to draft-illyes-webbotauth-jafar-01. |
| Resolve the prefix minimum and support advertisement issues | Open issues (Low) | No minimum for consumer bounds (§6.4); no authorization server metadata parameter. |

## Normative changes

- **Added:** the MUST that a consumer requiring an accepted set rejects the client's requests while it has none (§4.5); the SHOULD limiting use of an accepted set during failures (§4.5).
- **Broadened:** "MUST validate completely" now applies to any IP range set, not only a retrieved document; the failure MUST NOT names by-value metadata explicitly.
- **Changed:** the revalidation SHOULD uses the entity tag of the most recent retained complete response.
- **Moved:** the withdrawal MUST NOT from §4.4 to §4.5.
- **Removed (restates RFC 9111 §2):** the MUST NOT on reusing an entity tag across URIs. §4.4 still says a consumer does not reuse the previous URI's cached responses or validators, now citing Section 2 of RFC 9111. Also removed the list of cache directives.

## Not adopted

- **Scoping out the rejection error code:** kept as the one open issue. §5.1 already covers callers that have not authenticated. Scoping out the authenticated case leaves `invalid_client` as the default, which signals failed authentication and can trigger credential rotation. That is a question for the working group.
- **Reducing §5.1:** its public-client identification sentence came from the previous review and closes a real gap.
- **"The client associated with the request according to the consumer's trusted context":** vaguer than the text it would replace, so RS enforcement is scoped out instead.

Follow-up commits on this branch:
- Move the JAFAR discussion to a Related Work appendix.
- Define the accepted IP range set as the set in use, so that exceeding the staleness limit leaves no accepted set and the required-set rule applies.
- Revalidate a retained complete response rather than the latest response, which could be truncated (review of `aa8d761`).
- Replace "MUST NOT admit ... without regard to their source address", which allowed admitting every public address, with a direct MUST reject (review of `aa8d761`).

Build: 17 pages, citations resolved, idnits clean apart from the two known TOC false positives.

pulls.title: Editorial pass: tighten prose, separate implementation guidance
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Editorial pass: tighten the prose, make it easier to scan, keep normative keywords for interoperability and security, and move implementation and deployment guidance into a standard Implementation Considerations section. One commit per stage so any can be dropped.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Body words (Introduction–Privacy) | 3,502 | 3,336 (−5%) |
| Sentences with BCP 14 keywords | 48 | 42 |
| MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD / MAY | 18 / 16 / 10 / 6 | 18 / 15 / 9 / 3 |
| Pages | 17 | 18 (lists and new headings) |

## Commits

1. **Move implementation and deployment guidance out of the protocol sections** (relocation only, wording unchanged). New Implementation Considerations section, placed before Security Considerations as in the Client ID Metadata Document draft. It holds the enforcement points (firewall aggregate vs. per-client authorization server), the enterprise example, retrieval scheduling, gzip, and the CIMD 5 KB note. The staleness limit moved to Changes to Declared Ranges, IPv4-mapped conversion to Use, and the Shared Signals note to Related Work.
2. **Keep normative keywords for interoperability and security only.**
   - Duplicates: the Retrieval "MUST validate … MUST reject the entire document" moved into Acceptance (commit 5 restores its document-level scope); "and MUST NOT accept part of it" restated "MUST reject the entire document".
   - Merged: the failure and withdrawal MUST NOTs form one list in Failures and Withdrawal ("by itself" kept on withdrawal).
   - Demoted to statements: "array MAY contain both IPv4 and IPv6" (the type permits it), "Multiple clients MAY reference the same document" (a fact), the same-origin MAY (local policy), the gzip SHOULD (content negotiation).
   - Moved to Implementation Considerations: local minimum and maximum retrieval intervals; publisher allowance for approval delays.
3. **Compress prose and break dense paragraphs into lists.** Wording only; every BCP 14 sentence keeps its actor and condition. Matching is defined once, in Use. Restatements of RFC 9110 and RFC 9111 are dropped. The software statement precedence example is dropped because the rule covers it.
4. **Fix consistency issues from the post-edit read.**
   - Restores a 304 counting as a successful retrieval (dropped in commit 3).
   - Consumers enforce the *accepted* set.
   - "No declaration" means both parameters are absent.
   - The previous-URI rule applies only when the old metadata was by reference.
   - The SSRF URL comes from client metadata.
   - List leads fixed.
5. **Restore validation of the response and complete document** (review of `56e92e6`). Commit 2 narrowed "validate the response and the complete document" to "validate an IP range set", which misses document-level invalidity such as duplicate top-level members. Acceptance now keeps the set rule and adds: for a set obtained from a Client IP Range Document, the consumer MUST also validate the response and the complete document, and MUST reject the entire document if either is invalid.

## For the author

- The enterprise example moved from the Introduction to Implementation Considerations; the first review asked for it in the Introduction.
- The software statement / CIMD precedence example from the second review is removed.
- The Shared Signals scope sentence moved to Related Work.
- Section numbers shift: Security §7, Privacy §8, IANA §9, Examples §10.

## Verification

- `normative_diff.py` after each commit. Commit 1: no keyword change. Commit 2: exactly the removals listed above. Commits 3 and 4: rewording only. Commit 5: one added sentence (two MUSTs).
- A cold consistency reader checked every `{{anchor}}` pointer and dependency citation; all resolve to text that supports the citing sentence.
- Build clean apart from the known idnits table-of-contents false positives.

pulls.title: Fresh-eyes round: lifecycle limits, scope, response validity, and clarifications
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Combines the fresh-eyes critique (cold working-group and implementer reads) with the external review of `1c82988`. One commit per finding, so any can be dropped.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Body words (Introduction–Privacy) | 3,372 | 3,872 |
| Pages | 18 | 21 |
| MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD / MAY | 18 / 15 / 9 / 3 | 17 / 15 / 7 / 4 |

## Commits

| # | Commit | Source | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Limit use of an accepted set that no longer matches the declaration | Review 1; critique | The §7.2 limit now also covers withdrawal and a replacement not yet accepted, even when every retrieval succeeds. A consumer MAY narrow the accepted set to its intersection with a validated replacement. The availability trade-off is stated. |
| 2 | State the scope boundary and the purpose of declared ranges | Review 2; critique | Introduction: the metadata and consumer processing are specified; selecting clients, approving ranges, and configuring enforcement points are local policy. Resource server enforcement is out of scope. One sentence on what declared ranges add beyond client authentication. |
| 3 | Define a successful retrieval response | Critique | A 200 with `application/json` and a complete body within bounds, or a 304 to a conditional request. |
| 4 | Define prefix conformance by the RFC 9911 patterns | Critique | Platform parsers and the RFC 9911 patterns disagree (for example `192.0.2.0/024`), and one bad entry rejects the whole set. |
| 5 | Align two rules with the dependency text they cite | Critique | The duplicate-member rule becomes this draft's own (RFC 8259 §4 is a SHOULD). The certificate check is now "MUST NOT accept", strengthening RFC 9110 §4.3.4. RFC 8190 is cited for "globally reachable". |
| 6 | Separate registration from acceptance; name the pending state | Critique | Registering metadata does not accept the set. "awaits approval" becomes "not yet accepted under local policy". |
| 7 | Bound by-value sets; name the software statement error | Critique | The prefix-count bound applies to both forms. `invalid_software_statement` is named for trusted software statements. |
| 8 | Limit public-client enforcement to requests that present a grant | Review 4 | Requests with no grant, such as device authorization (RFC 8628 §3.1), are left unspecified. |
| 9 | Add a lifecycle summary table | Review 5 | A non-normative table in §4.6. |
| 10 | Add recovery, configuration endpoint, and refresh timing guidance | Review 5; critique | Administrative recovery path; enforcing at the RFC 7592 configuration endpoint can lock a client out; refresh when the freshness lifetime ends. |
| 11 | Explain the document model relative to JAFAR | Review 3 | Verified against JAFAR -01 §2.3: prefix objects, and consumers ignore an object with both or neither address member. Our model: one prefix array for both forms, whole-set rejection, association through client metadata. |
| 12 | Add redirect_uris to the Client ID Metadata Document example | Critique | Without `grant_types` the example defaults to `authorization_code`. |
| 13 | Demote keywords that restate dependencies or describe implementation | Critique (author approved) | The §2.3 consumer MUST and MUST NOT restate RFC 9911. "SHOULD detect unexpected expansion" becomes guidance. The If-None-Match mechanics move to §6.2. "reuse cached responses or validators" is dropped. |
| 14 | Fix consistency issues from the post-round read | Cold reader | The intersection MAY fits the acceptance model. One statement of the outcome after the limit. Table rows match the MAY. Wording fixes. |
| 15 | Allow an explicit policy decision to end rejection after the limit | Review of `678ae53` | After the limit, rejection continues until a new set is accepted or an explicit local policy decision removes the client from enforcement, so administrator discretion after a withdrawal does not depend on the timer. |

## Removed or demoted requirements

- **Restates a dependency:**
  - "Consumers MUST interpret each prefix by its network address and prefix length" and "MUST NOT treat a value as invalid solely because it is not in canonical format" (RFC 9911 §4: "must be accepted as a valid value, but it will be converted");
  - "SHOULD revalidate … If-None-Match" (RFC 9111 §4.3), now guidance in §6.2.
- **Undefined trigger, now guidance:** "SHOULD detect unexpected expansion".

## Unchanged, as already decided

Open Issues keeps one item (the error code). There is no minimum for consumer bounds. The enterprise example stays in §6, the precedence rule in §2.4, and the Shared Signals note in Related Work.

## Verification

- `normative_diff.py` after each commit. A cold consistency reader checked every touched cross-reference and the dependency citations; its findings are fixed in commit 14.
- Build clean apart from the known idnits table-of-contents false positives.

pulls.title: Adopt OAuth RFC conventions for prose and requirements
pulls.author: mcguinness

pulls.title: Tighten prose by removing repeated statements
pulls.author: mcguinness

pulls.title: Rename Section 4.5 to Continued Use
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Renames §4.5 from "Failures, Withdrawal, and Retention" to **Continued Use**. All three subsections govern whether the authorization server keeps using the accepted IP range set. The short form matches its sibling headings (Retrieval, Caching, Acceptance) under Retrieval and Acceptance.

- The subsections are 4.5.1 Failures, 4.5.2 Withdrawal, and 4.5.3 **Retention Limit** (was "Retention").
- The anchor changes from `retrieval-failures` to `continued-use`; nothing cited the old anchor.
- Headings only: the BCP 14 keyword sequence and all body text are unchanged.

pulls.title: Tighten Acceptance, Retention Limit, and Implementation Considerations
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies the agreed items from the second tightening review. Body text goes from 3,710 to 3,599 words (−3.0%) and 19 to 18 pages. The BCP 14 keyword sequence is unchanged.

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| §3 | Shared-document and hosting statements combined. |
| §4.3 | The required-set rule is stated generally ("while it has no accepted IP range set"). The list of reasons repeated other sections and omitted the case after the retention limit. |
| §4.5.3 | The three retention triggers are listed with "or". The prose "…, after …, and while …" could be read as requiring all three. |
| §6.1 | The enterprise example is halved. The recovery paragraph opens with the recovery path and keeps "a client whose source addresses move outside that set" (from the PR #4 review). |
| §6.3 | The rationale for independent bounds is dropped. |
| §7.1 | The same-origin option is its own paragraph. |

Not adopted, with reasons:
- Replacing the imported-term list with one sentence: RFC 9728 §1.2 and RFC 8414 §1.2 list the imported terms, so that is the OAuth convention.
- Bullets for the successful-response alternatives: the OAuth style pass used prose following RFC 8414 §3.2.
- Bullets for the software-statement meanings: the inline form is compact.
- Shortened example lead-ins: OAuth RFCs repeat "The following is a non-normative example" for each example.
- Also kept: the `jwks`/`jwks_uri` comparison and the companion-specification clause.

pulls.title: Keep enforcement outcomes in Use of Client IP Range Metadata
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Removes the overlap between §4 and §5. §4 now governs the accepted IP range set: validation, replacement, narrowing, failures, withdrawal, and the retention limit. §5 governs what enforcement does with it.

Two statements move into §5's paragraph on admission, after the matching rule:
- **the required-set MUST** (from §4.3 Acceptance);
- **the rejection after the retention limit**, with its explicit local policy exit (from §4.5.3, which now ends at the state change and points to §5).

That paragraph now covers every case: a matching address, an empty set, no set when one is required, after the retention limit, and otherwise local policy.

The failure and withdrawal MUST NOTs stay in §4.5.1 and §4.5.2, because they constrain the consequences of those events.

Requirements move verbatim, and the BCP 14 census is unchanged. Body text is 3,604 words (+5, from the two pointers).

pulls.title: Rename Sections 4.5, 5, and 5.1
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
"Continued Use" (§4.5) and "Use of Client IP Range Metadata" (§5) read as overlapping. This PR names each section for its job.

| Section | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 4.5 | Continued Use | **Retention** |
| 4.5.1 | Failures | **After a Failure** |
| 4.5.2 | Withdrawal | **After a Withdrawal** |
| 4.5.3 | Retention Limit | Retention Limit |
| 5 | Use of Client IP Range Metadata | **Enforcement** |
| 5.1 | Enforcement by Authorization Servers | **Client Identification and Error Responses** |

The §5.1 rename comes from the review of `bba26d0`: under Enforcement, the old title repeated its parent.

Headings only: the anchors, the body text, and the BCP 14 keyword sequence are unchanged.

pulls.title: Pre-publication fixes for -00
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies the pre-publication review: three cold reads (security directorate, implementer, document reviewer) plus the external review of `41fe7c1`. One commit per finding, so any can be dropped.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Body words (Introduction–Privacy) | 3,603 | 4,036 (+12%) |
| Pages | 19 | 21 |
| MUST / MUST NOT | 31 / 16 | 34 / 19 |

## Correctness and interoperability

| # | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Validate the stored response after a 304 | After a 304, the response and document checks apply to the stored response (RFC 9111 §4.3.4), so a body first served as `text/plain` cannot be accepted on revalidation. Conditional requests now cite RFC 9110 §13 instead of the non-normative §6.2. |
| 2 | Define update-request handling | An empty `client_ip_ranges` array in an RFC 7592 update declares an empty set and is not a deletion request (RFC 7592 §2.2 treats empty values as deletions). The 400 error rule now covers update requests. **MUST NOT** substitute a default for invalid client IP range metadata, which RFC 7592 §2.2 otherwise allows. |
| 3 | Require rejection after the retention limit | The three no-accepted-set cases are listed. Rejection after the limit is now a **MUST**, and "in other cases" is scoped. Relaxing after a withdrawal requires an explicit local policy decision. |
| 4 | Keep the CIMD SSRF rule from being overridden | Item 4's local policy exception does not override CIMD §8.6 for URLs from a Client ID Metadata Document. |
| 5 | Correct public-client identification | RFC 8628 §3.1 requires `client_id`, so the gap is authentication, not identification. Public clients are identified by the authorization code or refresh token. A source-address rejection does not count as a use of the authorization code (RFC 6749 §4.1.2). |
| 6 | Match no set when the source address cannot be determined | Covers §7.5's missing failure outcome. |
| 7 | Define when the retention limit runs | Each case gets a start event, and accepting a set under the current declaration ends the limit. A set narrowed to its intersection with the replacement is exempt from the third case. |

## Security and Privacy Considerations

| # | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | Extend Security and Privacy Considerations | New §7.3 Rejection Responses: a distinguishable rejection after authentication confirms stolen credentials are valid, and Open Issue 1 is updated to match. A document host can deny service to every client that shares the document. A declaration is not a client-side control. "Bound" becomes "limit". Privacy now covers a public CIMD that carries `client_ip_ranges`. |

## Clarity

| # | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | Clarify terms, wording, and one lowercase requirement | Defines "client IP range metadata" and drops "redirection endpoint". Uses URL consistently. "does not retrieve that URL again" becomes a **MUST NOT**. "While a validated replacement awaits acceptance" replaces "Before accepting". Adds "within its retention limit, if it sets one". Fixes the circular member reference in §3 and the redirection endpoints in §5. §6.1 uses the accepted set. Cites RFC 6454 for "origin". |
| 10 | State why now and the relation to sender-constrained tokens | Introduction: clients using CIMD reach authorization servers without prior registration, and ranges complement client authentication and sender-constrained tokens (RFC 9449, RFC 8705). Abstract: fixes "which supports" and mentions the processing rules. |
| 11 | Housekeeping before -00 | Anchors match headings (`retention`, `retention-limit`, `enforcement`, `client-identification`). Open Issues and Document History are marked for removal. The conditional request example gains `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. JAFAR wording is fixed. |

## Follow-up

| # | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | Fix consistency issues from the post-round read | **The departure from RFC 7592 §2.2 is now explicit:** the AS MUST NOT treat an empty `client_ip_ranges` array as a deletion request or ignore it. **The previous-URL MUST NOT applies only while the current metadata does not reference that URL.** A confirming retrieval, including a 304, ends the retention limit. A 304 with no stored response is a failure. Client identification adds the device code and the registration access token. The error-response open issue has one scope across §5.1, §7.3, and Appendix C. The accepted set is used where meant. The antecedent of "It MUST NOT" is fixed. |

## Requirement changes

- **Added:**
  - MUST (validate the stored response after a 304);
  - MUST NOT (no default substitution);
  - MUST NOT (do not retrieve the previous URL while the current metadata does not reference it);
  - MUST NOT (do not treat an empty array in an update as a deletion request, or ignore it).
- **Strengthened:** the rejection after the retention limit is now a MUST (was lowercase).
- **Scoped:** the update-request error now covers RFC 7592 updates.
- **Unchanged in meaning, reworded:** the narrowing MAY, the after-failure MAY, and the required-set MUST (now a list item).

## Kept as decided

- CIMD stays informative; the CIMD-specific text is conditional.
- The canonical-format MUST, the §7.2 MUST NOT, no minimum bounds, no AS metadata parameter, and strict `application/json` all stay.
- The "Web Authorization Protocol" header and the title are unchanged.

pulls.title: Cite BCP 14 as RFC 2119 and RFC 8174
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Switches `{::boilerplate bcp14-tagged-bcp14}` to `{::boilerplate bcp14-tagged}`. Requirements Notation now renders "BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174]", as RFC 8174 prescribes.

This clears the only idnits warning (`BCP14_CITED_INSTEAD_OF_RFCS`). The two remaining comments are not from the draft text: non-ASCII characters in fetched reference author names, and kramdown-rfc `<?line?>` markers. One-line change; no other text changes.
